# Digital Promises

> A book and blog on value, power, and risk in digital infrastructures at scale — provider/consumer separation, delegation to automation and AI, and how autonomous you can afford to be. Author: Peter van Eijk.

Every page on this site is also available as plain Markdown: append `index.md` to any page URL (e.g. `/book/act1-foundations/lunch-spain/index.md`), or use the `.md` link listed under each section below.

## The book

- [Book home](https://digitalinfrastructures.nl/book/): full table of contents across five acts.
- [Act I — What you stand on](https://digitalinfrastructures.nl/book/act1-foundations/): infrastructure fundamentals — storage, networks, processors, execution environments, cloud, promise theory.
- [Act II — Why the deal was good](https://digitalinfrastructures.nl/book/act2-value/): value of digital services, game theory, lock-in, buy/build/rent decisions.
- [Act III — Then the machines started promising](https://digitalinfrastructures.nl/book/act3-delegation/): automation, delegation, and AI agents.
- [Act IV — Who's in charge now](https://digitalinfrastructures.nl/book/act4-power/): power, governance, intermediaries, organization size.
- [Act V — Staying in control](https://digitalinfrastructures.nl/book/act5-risk/): risk management, controls, digital autonomy and sovereignty.

## Blog

- [Posts](https://digitalinfrastructures.nl/posts/): shorter pieces on cloud, AI, and digital infrastructure that haven't (yet) been folded into the book.
